name: Personal auto physical damage claim
summary: This process handles one first-party physical damage claim under a personal auto policy (collision or comprehensive) from the first notice of loss to payment and, where another driver was at fault, subrogation recovery. A call centre or app records the loss, the system checks coverage and assigns a desk adjuster, an appraiser writes the estimate, and the claim follows a repair, cash settlement or total loss path, with special investigations for suspicious claims. Most elapsed time is spent waiting for inspections, repair shop slots and parts, police reports, title and lien paperwork, and, for recoveries, the other insurer. State unfair claims practices rules set deadlines for acknowledgment, decisions and payment.

baseline.org_archetype: A US personal lines insurer insuring about one million private passenger vehicles, with a central claims contact centre, desk adjusters, staff and independent appraisers, a total loss unit, an SIU and a subrogation unit.
baseline.notes: Bodily injury and glass-only claims are routed to separate processes at first notice and are excluded; rental and towing are handled inside the claim.

unit_of_work: one personal auto physical damage claim (one insured vehicle)
trigger: A policyholder reports damage to or theft of an insured vehicle.
end_state: The claim is paid and closed, closed without payment, denied in writing, or, after payment, the subrogation recovery is collected or abandoned.

volume.seasonality: Higher in winter (ice and snow collisions, December to February) and in spring and summer hail seasons; deer collisions peak in October and November. Claim frequency fell in 2020 when driving dropped.

evidence.note: ISO/Verisk data show about 4.3 collision and 3.4 comprehensive claims per 100 car years in 2021; for about one million insured vehicles with glass-only claims removed this gives roughly 5,000 to 6,000 claims a month.

produces.to: State insurance fraud bureau (when fraud is suspected)

systems.name: Claims administration system (FNOL, reserves, diary, payments)
Collision estimating platform and photo-estimate app
Total loss valuation service (comparable vehicle reports)
Fraud scoring rules and industry claim history database

steps.name: Report loss
steps.description: The policyholder (or their agent) reports the accident, theft or weather damage by calling the claims line, through the agent, or in the insurer's mobile app or website, giving date, place, what happened, the vehicles and drivers involved and whether anyone was hurt.

error.defect_description: Facts incomplete or inaccurate (other party details missing, wrong date).

evidence.note: Insured's effort is not insurer labour, so touch is 0; the 75/25 phone versus digital split is an estimate for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record first notice of loss
steps.description: A claims call centre representative finds the policy, asks a scripted set of questions about the loss, vehicles, drivers, police report, injuries and where the vehicle is, types the answers into the claims system and explains next steps. Injury claims are split off to a bodily injury adjuster.

error.defect_description: Loss facts or vehicle details keyed wrongly; missed injury or second vehicle.

control.basis: Unfair claims settlement practices rules (NAIC Model 902 section 6): acknowledge a claim within 15 days

evidence.note: Acknowledgment rule from the NAIC model; call minutes and queue are author estimates.

steps.name: Verify policy and coverage
steps.description: The claims system checks that the policy was in force on the loss date, the vehicle is listed, the driver is not excluded and collision or comprehensive coverage applies, and loads the deductible. Mismatches such as an unlisted driver, a lapse for non-payment or late notice are flagged.

evidence.note: Automatic coverage verification was standard in claims systems of the period; the 7% question rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate coverage question
steps.description: An adjuster reviews the policy history, payment records and the facts, takes a statement about who was driving and for what purpose, and decides whether the loss is covered. Where coverage is doubtful but the investigation continues, a reservation of rights letter is sent.

control.basis: NAIC Model 900 section 4: no refusal to pay without a reasonable investigation; misrepresenting policy provisions is an unfair practice

evidence.note: Duty to investigate from the NAIC model act; times and outcome shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Triage, set reserve and assign claim
steps.description: Assignment rules in the claims system score the claim on damage description, drivability, likely total loss, liability complexity and fraud indicators, set an initial reserve and route it to a desk adjuster's queue, flagging suspicious claims for the special investigations unit.

error.defect_description: Misrouted claim (for example a likely total loss sent to the repair track).

control.basis: Statutory accounting: case reserves established for reported claims

evidence.note: Rule-based assignment and fraud scoring were common; the 3% early SIU referral rate is an author estimate (fraud is estimated at about 10% of P&C losses, most of it inflation rather than staged losses).

steps.name: Contact insured and take statement
steps.description: The assigned adjuster calls the insured within a business day, confirms the facts, takes a recorded statement when another party is involved, explains the deductible, rental coverage and inspection options (photo app, drive-in, preferred repair shop or field appraiser) and sets the appraisal.

error.defect_description: Key liability fact not asked or recorded.

control.basis: Carrier claim handling guideline: contact within 24 hours (supports NAIC Model 902 prompt acknowledgment and investigation)

next.condition: single-vehicle, theft, weather or clear facts

evidence.note: Contact standards are carrier guidelines that support the regulatory acknowledgment rule; times and the 50% multi-party share are author estimates.

steps.name: Request police report and other-party information
steps.description: For accidents involving another party, the adjuster orders the police report, contacts the other driver and their insurer to get their account and coverage details, and asks witnesses for statements. This runs alongside the vehicle appraisal.
outputs: requests to police, other driver and carrier

evidence.note: Standard liability investigation practice; author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for police report and other carrier's position
steps.description: The file waits for the police report, the other driver's statement and the other insurer's coverage and liability position. Only the part of this wait that outlasts the appraisal is counted here.

evidence.note: Police reports typically take days to weeks; the residual wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Determine liability
steps.description: The adjuster weighs the statements, police report, photos and state negligence rules, assigns a fault percentage to each driver, records the decision and notes subrogation potential when the other driver is at fault.

error.defect_description: Fault misjudged, losing a subrogation recovery or overpaying.

next.condition: inconsistent statements or other fraud indicators

evidence.note: Standard practice; minutes and SIU share are author estimates.

steps.name: Investigate SIU referral
steps.description: A special investigations unit investigator reviews the referral, checks prior claims, vehicle history and policy timing, may inspect the vehicle, interview witnesses or take an examination under oath, then clears the claim back to the adjuster or recommends denial. Suspected fraud is reported to the state fraud bureau.

error.defect_description: Legitimate claim delayed or a fraudulent one cleared.

control.basis: State insurance fraud statutes requiring an anti-fraud unit and reporting of suspected fraud to the state fraud bureau; California 2695.7(k) extends the decision limit to 80 days when fraud is suspected

evidence.note: Extended time limit for suspected fraud in the California rule; investigation minutes, queue and outcome shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Inspect vehicle and write damage estimate
steps.description: An appraiser inspects the vehicle in person at a drive-in centre, body shop or tow yard, or reviews photos the insured took in the app, then writes a line-by-line estimate in the estimating platform with parts, labour hours, paint and any prior damage noted. Preferred shops write the estimate themselves for the appraiser to review.

error.defect_description: Hidden damage not seen until teardown, or a likely total loss underestimated.

evidence.note: Appraiser duties from BLS; photo and virtual channels are tracked by CCC; minutes and the inspection wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Review estimate and decide repair or total loss
steps.description: The desk adjuster reviews the estimate against guidelines (labour rates, part types, repair versus replace), compares the repair cost with the vehicle's value and the state total loss threshold, and decides to authorise repair, pay the insured on the estimate, or move the claim to the total loss unit.
outputs: repair, cash settlement or total loss decision

error.defect_description: Borderline vehicle repaired when a total loss would have cost less, or the reverse.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8E: provide the insured a copy of the estimate; estimate must allow repair in a workmanlike manner

evidence.note: CCC reports the total loss share at roughly 15% to 25% by month in 2020-2024 (record 22.3% in 2024); 18% is used for 2019-2022. Other shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Authorize repair and arrange rental
steps.description: The adjuster sends the estimate and repair authorisation to the insured's chosen or preferred shop, books a rental car if the policy covers it, and diaries the file for the repair completion date.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8: insurer may not require the insured to use a particular repair shop

evidence.note: Shop choice rule from the NAIC model; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Shop tears down vehicle
steps.description: The insured drops the car at the shop when a slot is free; the shop disassembles the damaged area, finds any hidden damage and orders parts, sending a supplement request if more work is needed.

evidence.note: CCC reports supplements are common (56.3% of calibrations appear on a supplement); the 45% supplement share and shop scheduling wait are author estimates.

steps.name: Review supplement
steps.description: The appraiser reviews the shop's supplement photos and lines, re-inspects in person when the amount is large, agrees the added parts and labour, and updates the estimate; occasionally the added cost pushes the vehicle over the total loss threshold.

evidence.note: Supplement review practice; times and the total-loss conversion share are author estimates.

steps.name: Shop completes repairs
steps.description: The shop waits for parts, repairs, paints, reassembles, calibrates sensors and returns the car to the insured; parts shortages lengthened this period in 2021 and 2022.

evidence.note: CCC reports repair days rose after 2020 and remain 4-5 days above 2020; the 2 to 21 day range (mode 6) is an author estimate.

steps.name: Approve payment above authority
steps.description: A claims supervisor reviews payments above the adjuster's settlement authority, checking the estimate, supplements, coverage and liability notes, and approves or returns the payment.

control.basis: Carrier settlement authority limits by adjuster level

evidence.note: Authority limits are universal carrier practice; the share above authority and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Issue repair payment
steps.description: The adjuster checks the final invoice against the approved estimate and supplements, issues payment to the shop or jointly to the insured and lienholder less the deductible, sends the payment explanation and closes the rental.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 7: tender payment within 30 days of affirming liability; Model 900: state the coverage under which each payment is made

next.condition: other driver at fault: refer to subrogation

evidence.note: Payment rules from the NAIC models; the 30% subrogation share is an author estimate for collision and comprehensive mix.

steps.name: Value total loss
steps.description: A total loss specialist orders a comparable-vehicle valuation report, checks mileage, options and condition adjustments, adds applicable taxes and fees, subtracts the deductible and requests the lienholder's payoff amount.

error.defect_description: Valuation misses options or uses poor comparables.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8: total loss cash settlement based on the cost of comparable automobiles plus applicable taxes and fees

evidence.note: Valuation standard from the NAIC model; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present total loss offer and negotiate
steps.description: The specialist calls the insured, explains the valuation report and sends a copy, answers objections and, when the insured supplies better comparables or option details, re-runs the valuation.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8: settlement basis and deductions disclosed to the insured in writing

evidence.note: Dispute share and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for title and lien documents
steps.description: The file waits while the insured signs the title and power of attorney, hands over keys, and the lender sends the payoff letter and releases the lien; out-of-state titles and slow lenders add weeks.

evidence.note: Author estimate of title and lienholder turnaround.

steps.name: Pay total loss settlement and assign salvage
steps.description: A claims clerk checks the signed title and payoff letter, issues payment to the lienholder and the remainder to the insured, and assigns the vehicle to the salvage auction vendor for pickup and sale.

error.defect_description: Payoff amount or payee keyed wrongly.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 7: tender payment within 30 days of affirming liability

next.condition: other driver at fault: refer to subrogation

evidence.note: Payment rule from the NAIC model; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft claim denial
steps.description: The adjuster drafts the denial letter citing the specific policy provision, condition or exclusion that applies and the facts relied on, and sends it with the file for supervisory review.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 7: denial in writing referencing the specific policy provision

evidence.note: Requirement stated in the NAIC model; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Review and send denial
steps.description: A claims supervisor reads the file and draft, confirms the investigation was reasonable and the provision applies, then approves and sends the letter or reverses the decision.

control.basis: Carrier policy: supervisory approval of claim denials (manages unfair practices and bad-faith exposure)

evidence.note: Supervisory denial review is common practice; reversal share and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Send subrogation demand
steps.description: A subrogation specialist reviews the liability decision, assembles the estimate, photos, payments and police report, and sends a demand to the at-fault driver's insurer for the amount paid plus the insured's deductible.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8D: include the insured's deductible in subrogation demands on request

evidence.note: Deductible rule from the NAIC model; Arbitration Forums reports about 2.3 million subrogation demands a year; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for at-fault carrier response
steps.description: The demand waits in the other insurer's queue until it accepts liability and pays, offers a compromise, disputes fault, or turns out to have no coverage for its driver.

evidence.note: Response times and outcome shares are author estimates.

steps.name: File inter-company arbitration
steps.description: The specialist files the disputed demand with the inter-company arbitration forum, uploads evidence and argument, and waits for the arbitrator's decision.

error.defect_description: Weak evidence package loses a winnable case.

next.condition: award in our favour (full or partial)

evidence.note: Arbitration Forums runs an automobile subrogation arbitration programme with about 1.1 million disputes a year; times and win share are author estimates.

steps.name: Record recovery and refund deductible
steps.description: The specialist posts the recovery to the claim, refunds the insured's deductible in proportion to the recovery, and closes the file.

control.basis: NAIC Model 902 section 8D: share subrogation recoveries proportionately with the insured

evidence.note: Proportionate sharing rule stated in the NAIC model; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Coverage question
exceptions.description: Unlisted or excluded driver, lapse for non-payment, business use or late notice; the adjuster investigates and may deny.

exceptions.name: SIU referral
exceptions.description: Fraud indicators at intake or inconsistent statements send the claim to the special investigations unit.

exceptions.name: Supplement after teardown
exceptions.description: The shop finds hidden damage after disassembly and the appraiser must approve added work.

exceptions.name: Total loss
exceptions.description: Repair cost exceeds the threshold share of the vehicle's value; the claim moves to valuation, negotiation, title transfer and salvage.

exceptions.name: Valuation dispute
exceptions.description: The insured rejects the total loss value and supplies other comparables, so the valuation is re-run.

exceptions.name: Disputed subrogation
exceptions.description: The other insurer disputes liability and the demand goes to inter-company arbitration.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from first notice of loss to claim closure (including subrogation recovery where pursued)
benchmarks.population: US personal auto physical damage claims, 2019-2022

evidence.note: No source opened gives a measured FNOL-to-closure median. Estimate: repairable claims about 2 to 4 weeks (inspection, shop scheduling and repair of 1 to 3 weeks, with repair days rising after 2020 per CCC), total losses 3 to 5 weeks, subrogation adding 2 to 6 months for about a quarter of claims, all within the NAIC 15/21/30-day handling limits.

benchmarks.population: NAIC Model 902 (states adopt variants; California uses 15/40/30)

evidence.note: Stated in the model regulation and the California rule.
Stated in the III table.
Stated in the Crash Course report.
Stated by the Coalition Against Insurance Fraud, without a year.

pain_points.description: Repairable claims wait for shop slots, teardown and parts, and nearly half need a supplement approval mid-repair, so the insured is in a rental for weeks.

evidence.note: CCC reports longer repair days after 2020 and frequent supplements.

pain_points.description: Total loss settlements stall on title, power of attorney and lienholder payoff letters, while storage fees accrue at the tow yard.

evidence.note: Author judgement from common practice.

pain_points.description: Liability decisions wait for police reports and the other insurer's response, and subrogation demands then wait months in other carriers' queues or arbitration.

evidence.note: Arbitration Forums handles about 1.1 million inter-company disputes a year.

pain_points.description: Desk adjusters carry high pending caseloads, so first contact, estimate review and payment each wait in a queue, and claim facts are re-typed between the FNOL record, estimating platform and payments.

evidence.note: Author judgement.

assumptions: External steps (insured, repair shop, police, other insurer) carry zero touch time; their effort is inside the waits, so the staffing comparison reflects insurer labour only.
Liability investigation runs alongside the appraisal in practice; the sequential model counts only the part of the police-report wait that outlasts the appraisal.

Shares for repair (62%), cash settlement on the estimate (18%), total loss (18% at estimate, plus supplements that convert) and subrogation referral (25-30% of paid claims) are author estimates; the total loss share is anchored on CCC's 15-25% monthly range.
The cycle-time benchmark is an author estimate because the measured sources (J.D. Power, CCC repair cycle studies) were not reachable or report only partial intervals; treat it as tier C.
Salvage sale after the total loss payment is treated as a downstream process and does not hold the claim open in this model.
Appraiser time for field inspections includes travel; independent appraiser fees are treated as labour at the staff appraiser rate.
Stated FTEs are about 15% above the hands-on time implied at 130 productive hours a month, covering diary reviews, inbound status calls and reserve updates not modelled as steps.

Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 hourly wage x 1.49 (benefits: wages are 67% of compensation in financial activities, which includes insurance, BLS ECEC Dec 2021) x 1.2 for overhead (author estimate), about 1.8 x wage.
